title: Cash flows growing 3% discounted at 9%
caption: Adding the present value of each year's cash flow, starting with £10m/1.09 in year 1, the total climbs towards C₁/(r − g) = 10/0.06 = £166.7m: later years add less and less.
alt: A rising curve over 100 years that levels off just below £166.7m.
description: Year t's cash flow is 10 × 1.03^(t−1), discounted by 1.09^t.
The running total after n years is 10/(0.09 − 0.03) × (1 − (1.03/1.09)^n).
As n grows it settles at £166.7m, the value of the firm.
